info.title: tocsin
info.description: Uptime monitor, status page and release log. Reads are public; writes need a `[[token]]` with the route's scope, and a `status:read` token also sees non-public projects, check targets and raw check results.

get.summary:
Every alert sent to a notifier that fired at any moment in the window,
newest start first, with the labels its messages carry and how each
message's delivery went.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
The start of the window (RFC 3339): alerts still firing at or after
it. At most 366 days ago; default 30 days ago. Keep it the same
while paging. A firing alert is always kept; a resolved one only
while one of its deliveries is, so resolved alerts reach back no
further than delivery retention.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description:
Only alerts after the previous page's last: its `next_before`. One
that names no alert of this read (pruned since, or from a read with
another `state`) is 422; start again without it.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only `firing` or only `resolved` alerts; default both.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

422.description: A bad `since`, `limit` or `state`, or a `before` naming no alert of this read

get.summary:
Every check and heartbeat on a public component with its current
state; with a `status:read` token, those on no component or on one that
is not public too.

401.description: An `Authorization` header with an unknown token

get.summary: One check's or heartbeat's raw results, newest first.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
The start of the window (RFC 3339): at most 366 days ago; default
one day ago. Keep it the same while paging.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description:
Only results after the previous page's last: its `next_before`.
One that names no result of this check (purged since, or from
another read) is 422; start again without it.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

422.description: A bad `since` or `limit`, or a `before` naming no row of this read

get.summary:
One component: its status, its checks and heartbeats, and the open
incidents naming it.

401.description: An `Authorization` header with an unknown token

404.description: No `[[component]]` has that id, or it is not public and the token lacks `status:read`

get.summary:
When the running configuration was loaded, and whether the last reload
put its configuration in place. After a failed one, `ok` is false,
`errors` says why, and the configuration from `loaded_at` is still
running.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

get.summary:
Every event from now on, as server-sent events: the event name is the
event's `type` and the data its JSON. The first event is `resync`, and
so is the one after the stream fell behind and missed some; on either,
re-read what you show. A comment line every 15 seconds keeps a quiet
connection open. Anyone sees incident events, changes of public
components and of the checks and heartbeats on one, and releases of
public projects; a `status:read` token sees every component, check and
release. Without one, the stream ends when the configuration reloads,
since what is public may have changed; reconnect to follow the new one.

401.description: An `Authorization` header with an unknown token

get.summary: Record a ping, for clients that can only send `GET`; the same as `POST`.

schema.description: What a job reports about its own run.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description:
A `[[token]]` secret with the `heartbeat` scope, for clients that
cannot send `Authorization: Bearer`, percent-encoded (a bare `+`
reads as a space). The header wins when both are sent. A URL carrying
its token is itself a secret: it may be logged on its way here, and a
link checker or chat unfurler that fetches it pings. Prefer the
header.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: A short note stored with the result, such as what failed; at most 1024 bytes.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

422.description: A bad `status`, or a `message` over 1024 bytes

post.summary: Record a ping: the job ran, and says whether it succeeded.

schema.description: What a job reports about its own run.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description:
A `[[token]]` secret with the `heartbeat` scope, for clients that
cannot send `Authorization: Bearer`, percent-encoded (a bare `+`
reads as a space). The header wins when both are sent. A URL carrying
its token is itself a secret: it may be logged on its way here, and a
link checker or chat unfurler that fetches it pings. Prefer the
header.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: A short note stored with the result, such as what failed; at most 1024 bytes.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

422.description: A bad `status`, or a `message` over 1024 bytes

get.summary:
List incidents and maintenance, newest first. Drafts, and each
incident's `internal_note` and `external_key`, are listed only to a
`status:read` token; so is `?external_key=`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only incidents with a smaller id: the previous page's `next_before`.

parameters.name: external_key
parameters.description:
Only the incidents given this `external_key` at creation, draft or
published, open or resolved, newest first and paged like the rest:
at most one is open, and each resolved one is an earlier episode.
Needs a `status:read` token.

401.description: An `Authorization` header with an unknown token

post.summary:
Open an incident or announce scheduled maintenance, published or as a
draft. `draft` left out publishes for an `incident` token and drafts
for an `incident:draft` one. With an `external_key` an open incident
already has, nothing is written and that incident is answered with
200, as a release posted again is; a resolved incident has freed its
key, so the key then opens a new incident with 201. The answer carries `internal_note`
and `external_key` only for a token that also has `status:read`.

200.description: An open incident already has this `external_key`: that incident, unchanged; `Location` names it

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

403.description: The token has neither incident scope, or asks to publish (`"draft": false`) with only `incident:draft`

422.description: Invalid fields, by path; an `external_key` with a terminal first `status`

get.summary:
One incident with every update. A draft, and the `internal_note` and
`external_key`, are shown only to a `status:read` token.

401.description: An `Authorization` header with an unknown token

delete.summary:
Discard a draft: delete it with its updates. A published incident is
never deleted. Answers the draft as it was.

200.description: Discarded; the draft as it was

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

403.description: The token has neither incident scope

patch.summary:
Change the title, impact, components, schedule or internal note. Fields
left out are unchanged; status changes only through an update. An
`incident:draft` token may edit only a draft. The answer carries
`internal_note` and `external_key` only for a token that also has
`status:read`.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

403.description: The token has neither incident scope, or only `incident:draft` and the incident is published

post.summary:
Publish a draft: show it publicly from now on and announce it to
subscribers once, as if it had just been opened. Needs the `incident`
scope; `incident:draft` never publishes.

requestBody.description: Optional; left out, subscribers are notified

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

post.summary:
Append an update, moving the incident to its status. An
`incident:draft` token may update only a draft.

201.description: Appended; the incident with the new update last

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

403.description: The token has neither incident scope, or only `incident:draft` and the incident is published

422.description: Invalid fields, by path; a `status` that reopens a resolved incident whose `external_key` another open incident now holds

get.summary:
Outages open at any moment in the window, newest start first: of
checks and heartbeats on a public component, and with a `status:read`
token of every check.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
The start of the window (RFC 3339): outages still open at or after
it. At most 366 days ago; default 30 days ago. Keep it the same
while paging.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description:
Only outages after the previous page's last: its `next_before`.
One that names no outage (purged since) is 422; start again
without it.

401.description: An `Authorization` header with an unknown token

422.description: A bad `since` or `limit`, or a `before` naming no row of this read

get.summary:
Published releases, newest first. Without a `status:read` token only
public projects' releases are listed.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description:
Only this project's releases. A project the reader may not see
matches nothing, like one that does not exist.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only releases published at or after this instant (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description:
Only releases older than the previous page's last: its
`next_before`.

401.description: An `Authorization` header with an unknown token

post.summary:
Publish a release. Posting the same project, version and environment
again updates it in place: title, notes and url are replaced,
`released_at` moves only later, and a deploy already stamped is kept.

200.description: Already recorded (published, or stamped as deployed); updated

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

422.description: Invalid fields, by path; an unknown project is named

post.summary:
Record that a version was deployed, at `deployed_at` or now. The body
may be empty. A version not yet published is recorded as a stub that
its publish fills in; until then it is on the timeline but not in the
release log.

201.description: Not yet published: recorded as a stub

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

422.description: Invalid fields, by path; an unknown project is named

get.summary:
Silences, newest first, active or over, each with the messages it held
back.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description:
Only silences older than the previous page's last: its
`next_before`.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

post.summary:
Silence the alerts the matchers name until `expires_at`. Every matcher
given must equal the alert's; at least one, or an `episode`, is
required. With an `episode` (an outage id) the silence also ends when
that outage does, and the matchers default to its node and subject.
`expires_at` is required and at most `[server] max_silence` away; who
made the silence is the token, never a field.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

422.description: Invalid fields, by path: no `expires_at`, one past `max_silence`, an unknown subject, or an episode that has ended

get.summary: One silence, with the newest messages it held back.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

post.summary:
End a silence now, before it expires. One already over is answered as
it is; a silence is never extended.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

get.summary: The page's overall status, every component's, and the open incidents.

401.description: An `Authorization` header with an unknown token

get.summary: List subscribers, oldest first, with the totals.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only subscribers with a larger id: the previous page's `next_after`.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

404.description: Subscriptions are off on this server

post.summary:
Sign up for email about incidents and releases. The answer is the same
whether the address is new, waiting for confirmation or already
subscribed; only the email it then receives differs.

404.description: Subscriptions are off on this server

422.description: Invalid fields, by path, or a failed Turnstile check

429.description: Too many sign-ups from this client or for this address; `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The Turnstile answer could not be checked

delete.summary: Remove a subscriber at once, with every delivery still queued for them.

401.description: No token, or an unknown one

404.description: No subscriber has that id, or subscriptions are off

get.summary:
Outages, incidents and deploys, oldest first, read in one snapshot.
Ties on time order by kind (outage, incident, deploy, release), then id.
Without a `status:read` token only public projects' deploys appear,
and only outages of checks and heartbeats on a public component; a
component that is not public answers as an unknown one.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description:
Only events touching this `[[component]]`: outages of its checks,
incidents naming it, deploys of projects that list it.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
The start of the window (RFC 3339): at most 366 days ago; default
30 days ago. Keep it the same while paging.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only events after the previous page's last: its `next_after`.

401.description: An `Authorization` header with an unknown token

422.description: An unknown component, or a bad `since`, `after` or `limit`

Actor.description: Who wrote a change: recorded with every incident, update and edit.

id.description: The token's id, or the person's identity from the proxy.

AlertDelivery.description: One message queued for an alert, and how its delivery went.

oneOf.description:
When it was delivered, given up on or held back; `null` while
pending.

health.description: The alert's health when it was queued.

last_error.description:
The last failed attempt's error, secrets redacted; `null` if none
failed.

silence_id.description: The silence that held it back, if one did.

AlertHistory.description: `GET /api/v1/alerts/history`: one page of alerts, newest first.

next_before.description:
Pass as `before`, with the same `since` and `state`, for the next
page; `null` on the last.

since.description: The start of the window: alerts still firing at or after it.

AlertRecord.description:
One notifier's alert for one check or heartbeat on one node, from fire
to resolve.

annotations.description:
The subject's configured annotations as they were when it opened.
An Alertmanager message adds `summary`, `description` and the rest.

attempted.description:
Whether a send of a fire or repeat was ever started, whatever came
of it. Until one was, its notifier cannot have heard of it.

component_id.description: The subject's component when it last fired, if any.

deliveries.description:
Every message queued for it that delivery retention still keeps,
oldest first.

oneOf.description: When it ended; `null` while it fires.
Why it ended; `null` while it fires.

labels.description:
The labels every Alertmanager message of it carries, fire, repeat
and resolve alike: the subject's configured labels as they were when
it opened, its `class`, and `alertname`, `node`, `subject_kind` and
`subject_id`. Other notifiers get the same identity.

notified.description:
Whether its notifier has accepted a fire or repeat for its current
fire, the one for its latest outage or health. A long-firing alert
can outlive its deliveries, so this says what they no longer can.

notifier_id.description: The notifier it was sent to.

route_id.description: The route that sent it there.

started_at.description: When the outage it first fired for started.

subject_kind.description: Whether `subject_id` is a check or a heartbeat.

CheckKind.description: Whether a member of a component is probed or pinged.

checks.description: Checks, then heartbeats, each in configuration order.

detail.description:
How each assertion fared, as `tocsin probe run` reports it.
Diagnostic: its shape may change between versions.

error.description: Why it failed, when it did.

status_code.description: The protocol status code, when the check has one (HTTP).

CheckResults.description:
`GET /api/v1/checks/{id}/results`: one page of raw results, newest
first.

next_before.description:
Pass as `before`, with the same `since`, for the next page; `null`
on the last.

since.description: The start of the window: results that started at or after it.

CheckState.description: One check or heartbeat and its current state.

oneOf.description: Its confirmed health; `null` until confirmed.

id.description:
Its id. Checks and heartbeats share one id space, so this names
one member and its results alike.

interval.description:
How often it runs, or how often a heartbeat expects a ping, such
as `30s` or `1h30m`.

oneOf.description: Its latest result's health, which may not be confirmed yet.
When its latest result started.

name.description: Its display name: the id when none is configured.

oneOf.description: Since when it has had that health.

target.description:
What a check probes. Only with a `status:read` token, since it can
name internal hosts; absent otherwise and for heartbeats.

topology_node.description:
The node it watches in the estate's map, as configured. Only with a
`status:read` token, since an id can name internal hosts; absent
otherwise and when none is set.

type.description:
The probe a check runs (`http`, `tcp`, `dns`, `icmp`, `tls`);
`null` for a heartbeat.

ComponentDetail.description:
`GET /api/v1/components/{id}`: one component, its checks and the open
incidents naming it.

checks.description: The checks and heartbeats that set its health.

incidents.description: Open incidents and maintenance naming it, newest first.

ComponentState.description: One `[[component]]` and what the status page shows for it.

oneOf.description: Its health from its checks alone; `null` until one reports.

status.description:
What the status page shows: its checks' health, overridden by
incidents and maintenance. `unknown` until a check reports.

ComponentStatus.description: What the status page shows for a component.

ConfigStatus.description:
How the configuration last reloaded, as `GET /api/v1/config/status`
returns it.

errors.description:
Why the last attempt failed, each with its file, line and column
when it has one; empty when it did not fail.

last_attempt_at.description:
When a reload was last tried, whether or not it took; the startup
read until the first.

loaded_at.description:
When the running configuration was read: at startup, or by the
last reload that put its configuration in place.

ok.description:
Whether the last attempt put its configuration in place. False
means the configuration from `loaded_at` is still running.

DeployStamp.description:
`POST /api/v1/releases/{project}/{version}/deployed`: record that a
version was deployed. The body may be empty.

oneOf.description:
Defaults to now; at most an hour past the server's clock. The
release keeps the latest deploy time it is given, so a stamp
earlier than the recorded one changes nothing.

Diagnostic.description:
One configuration error, located as precisely as the problem allows.

Serialized with every key present (`null` when unknown), so a reader can
rely on the shape: `{file, line, column, path, message, hint}`.

file.description:
The file, as the loader named it; absent for a problem with the
folder as a whole, such as a missing setting no file mentions.

hint.description: How to fix it, when there is something more to say.

path.description: Where in the file's data the problem is, such as `check[2].timeout`.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response.

fields.description: For `invalid`: every problem, by path in the request.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person.

FieldError.description: One problem with a request, at a field path such as `components[1]`.

path.description: Where in the request body; empty for the body as a whole.

Health.description: How a check fared. Ordered from best to worst, so `max` is the worst.

HeldKind.description: Which message a silence held back.

HeldMessage.description:
One message a silence held back: the alert still fired (or resolved)
and is recorded; only the sending was skipped.

delivery_id.description: The delivery's id in the outbox.

health.description: The alert's health when the message was queued.

node.description: The node that saw the alert.

Impact.description: How badly the affected components are hit. Ordered least to worst.

Incident.description: An incident or scheduled maintenance, with every update.

external_key.description:
The key its creator gave it, such as an alert cluster's. Present
only where `internal_note` would be, and only when set.

impact.description: How badly the affected components are hit.

internal_note.description:
Notes for the people who run it: evidence, links. Never public,
before or after publishing. Present only to a `status:read` token
and in the admin, and only when set.

kind.description: Incident or maintenance. Fixed at creation.

oneOf.description:
When it was published: shown publicly and announced to subscribers.
`null` while it is a draft, which only trusted readers see.
Who published it; `null` while it is a draft.

When the latest update moved it to `resolved` or `completed`; cleared
if a later update reopens it.
When maintenance is planned to end; after `scheduled_start`.

When maintenance is planned to begin; always set for maintenance,
never for an incident.

status.description: The status of the latest update.

title.description: One line, shown on the status page.

updated_at.description: When it last changed: an update or an edit.

updates.description: Every update, oldest first. The first is the opening message.

IncidentEdit.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/incidents/{id}`: change what an incident says. Only the
fields given change; status changes only through an update.

components.description: The full new set of affected components (not a delta).

oneOf.description: A new impact.

internal_note.description:
A new internal note, replacing the old one; empty clears it. Never
shown publicly.

oneOf.description: A new planned end. Maintenance only.
A new planned start. Maintenance only.

title.description: A new title, not empty, at most 200 characters.

IncidentKind.description: Whether something broke or work was planned.

IncidentList.description: `GET /api/v1/incidents`: one page of incidents, newest first.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to get the next page; `null` on the last page.

IncidentStatus.description:
Where an incident or maintenance stands. The first four belong to
incidents, the last three to maintenance; see
[`IncidentStatus::allowed_for`].

IncidentUpdate.description: One entry in an incident's timeline. Updates are never changed.

status.description: The status the incident moved to (or stayed at).

Matchers.description:
Which alerts a silence holds back: every field set must equal the
alert's. A field left out matches anything.

component.description:
A `[[component]]` id: the alert's subject's component when it last
fired.

node.description: The node that saw the alert, as its `[server] node_id`.

oneOf.description: Whether `subject` names a check or a heartbeat.

NewIncident.description: `POST /api/v1/incidents`: open an incident or announce maintenance.

components.description: Ids of configured components. May be empty.

draft.description:
`true` saves it as a draft: internal only, announced to nobody, until
a person publishes it. Left out, it is published when the caller may
publish (the `incident` scope, or a person) and a draft otherwise
(the `incident:draft` scope); the MCP tool always defaults to a
draft.

external_key.description:
The caller's own key for what it reports, such as an alert
cluster's: one line, at most 200 characters, set at creation only.
A create repeating the key of an open incident answers that incident
with 200 and changes nothing; resolving it, or discarding a draft,
frees its key. A keyed incident must open non-terminal.

internal_note.description:
Notes for whoever publishes it: evidence, links. Not empty. Never
shown publicly, before or after publishing; read back only with the
`status:read` scope.

message.description: The first update, in markdown. Not empty.

notify.description:
Whether subscribers hear about it. `false` opens it quietly. It
changes nothing else.

oneOf.description:
Required for maintenance, after `scheduled_start`; refused for an
incident.
Required for maintenance, refused for an incident.

The first update's status. Defaults to `investigating` for an
incident and `scheduled` for maintenance.

title.description: One line, not empty, at most 200 characters.

NewRelease.description:
`POST /api/v1/releases`: publish a release, or update the one with the
same project, version and environment.

oneOf.description:
When it was deployed, if it already has been. Left as recorded when
omitted or earlier than the recorded time; never more than an hour
past the server's clock.

environment.description:
Defaults to `production`. 1 to 32 characters, the same set as
`version`.

notes.description: Markdown, at most 64 KiB. Defaults to none.

oneOf.description:
When it was released. Defaults to now on the first publish and to
the recorded time on a re-publish; it may move later, never earlier,
and never more than an hour past the server's clock.

title.description: One line, at most 200 characters. Defaults to the version.

url.description: An `http` or `https` link to the release.

version.description:
1 to 64 characters: ASCII letters, digits and `.`, `_`, `+`, `-`,
starting with a letter or digit, such as `v1.4.0` or `2026.10.23+5`.

NewSilence.description:
`POST /api/v1/silences`: hold back the alerts `matchers` names until
it expires, or until outage `episode` closes if that is sooner.

episode.description:
An outage id: the silence ends when that outage closes (the
subject recovers, or moves between degraded and down), so a
re-fire is sent. The outage must be open.

oneOf.description:
When it stops applying: in the future, and at most `[server]
max_silence` from now. Give this or `expires_in`, not both.

expires_in.description:
How long from now it applies, such as `"30m"` or `"1h30m"`, counted
from the server's clock: at most `[server] max_silence`. Give this
or `expires_at`, not both.

matchers.description:
Which alerts it holds back. At least one field unless `episode` is
set, which fills in the outage's node, subject kind and subject.

reason.description: Why: shown wherever the silence is.

components.description:
Components whose incidents to hear about, or `["*"]` for every one.
Default `["*"]`.

email.description:
The address to send to. It receives only a confirmation until its
owner follows the link in it.

projects.description:
Public projects whose releases to hear about, or `["*"]` for every
one. Default none.

turnstile.description:
The Cloudflare Turnstile answer, required when the server has
Turnstile on.

notify.description:
Whether email subscribers hear about it. `false` posts it quietly,
for a typo fix or a minor note. It changes nothing else.

status.description: The status the incident moves to; it must suit the incident's kind.

OutageList.description: `GET /api/v1/outages`: one page of outages, newest first.

next_before.description:
Pass as `before`, with the same `since`, for the next page; `null`
on the last.

since.description: The start of the window: outages still open at or after it.

OutageRecord.description: A machine-detected outage: a check confirmed degraded or down.

component_id.description: The check's component when the outage opened, if any.

oneOf.description: When it ended; `null` while it is open.
How it ended; `null` while it is open.

subject_kind.description: Whether `check_id` is a check or a heartbeat.

received_at.description:
When the ping was recorded; the next is due by this plus the
heartbeat's `interval + grace`.

PingStatus.description: What a job reports about its own run.

Publish.description:
`POST /api/v1/incidents/{id}/publish`: whether subscribers hear about
it. The body may be left out.

notify.description: `false` publishes it quietly: shown publicly, announced to nobody.

Release.description: A release of a project to one environment.

created_at.description: When tocsin first heard of it.

oneOf.description:
When it was last deployed, if it has been: the latest deploy time
it has been given.

environment.description: Where it was released, such as `production` or `staging`.

notes.description: Markdown. Empty when none were given.

oneOf.description:
When it was published. `null` for a deploy stamped before its
publish; never moved earlier once set.

title.description:
One line. Empty while the release is only a deploy stamp waiting
for its publish.

url.description: A link to the release, such as its tag or changelog.

version.description: The version, as CI named it.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to get the next, older page; `null` on the last.

releases.description: Newest `released_at` first, ties by newest id.

SignupAccepted.description: The answer to a sign-up, the same for every address.

Silence.description: A silence and what it held back.

created_by.description:
Who made it: the caller the server authenticated, never a name
the request gave.

oneOf.description: When someone ended it early, if they did.
Who ended it early.

episode.description: The outage it is scoped to, if any.

oneOf.description: When its episode's outage closed, if it has.

held.description:
The messages it held back, newest first: at most the latest 100.
Kept as long as failed deliveries are.

held_total.description:
How many messages it held back that are still kept, including any
past the 100 in `held`.

state.description: Whether it applies now, as of the request.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to get the next page; `null` on the last page.

SilenceState.description: Whether a silence holds back alerts now, and if not, what ended it.

StatusDocument.description: `GET /api/v1/status.json`: everything a status page shows right now.

generated_at.description: When the server read the status.

incidents.description:
Incidents not yet resolved and maintenance not yet completed,
scheduled ones included, newest first.

status.description:
The worst component status: operational, unknown, maintenance,
degraded, down, in that order; unknown with no components.

SubscriberEntry.description: One subscriber, as an operator sees them.

components.description: Components whose incidents they hear about; `*` is every one.

oneOf.description: When they confirmed; absent while they have not.

projects.description: Projects whose releases they hear about; `*` is every public one.

SubscriberList.description: One page of subscribers, in id order, with the totals.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last.

Timeline.description: `GET /api/v1/timeline`: outages, incidents and deploys, oldest first.

events.description:
Oldest first; ties by kind (outage, incident, deploy, release),
then id.

next_after.description:
Pass as `after`, with the same `since`, to get the next page;
`null` on the last.

since.description: The start of the window: events at or after it.

truncated.description: Whether more events fell in the window than `limit`.

oneOf.description: A check failed: at the outage's start.

component_id.description: The check's component when the outage opened, if any.

oneOf.description: When it ended; `null` while it is open.
How it ended; `null` while it is open.

subject_kind.description:
Whether `check_id` is a check or a heartbeat; `kind` is the
event's.

oneOf.description: An incident or maintenance was opened: at its creation.
A release was deployed: at `deployed_at`.
A release was published and not yet deployed: at `released_at`.

TimelineEvent.description:
One entry on the timeline. Every kind carries `at`, the instant it is
placed at, and the `id` of its row.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339; written in UTC with millisecond precision, read with any offset.
